prompt: Parse log lines shaped like "[LEVEL] message" with a capturing group, then use that parser to count ERROR lines. Complete parseLevel and countErrors in LogParser.
explanation: Square brackets are regex metacharacters, so literal brackets are written \[ and \] (doubled backslashes inside the Java string). Parentheses create capturing group 1 around [A-Z]+, and after a successful matches() call, m.group(1) returns just the text that group matched -- the level without its brackets. countErrors then reuses parseLevel, which keeps the regex in exactly one place.
hints: The brackets in the line are literal characters, but [ and ] mean something in regex -- escape them as \\[ and \\] in the Java string.
Wrap the level in parentheses to capture it: "\\[([A-Z]+)\\] .*" -- then m.group(1) is the level.
matches() must consume the whole line; call it before group(1), and have countErrors loop calling parseLevel and comparing with .equals("ERROR").
